items.issue: Sections0/6 call T a reduction to the seed problem.
items.correction: TheoremS supplies a sufficient condition for dimension drop and singularity. Necessity or equivalence with T is not established; failure of seeds would not refute T.

items.issue: Section6 says products cannot supply a seed and any successful seed must avoid reflection doubling.
items.correction: These conclusions do not follow from the explicitly heuristic exponent count. No requisite Diophantine lower bound for the actual pair of Salem angles, uniform all-product obstruction or exclusion of favorable constants/exceptional approximations has been proved. Preserve as heuristic only.

items.issue: PropositionO2 is summarized as unconditional action doubling per factor.
items.correction: Retain only its displayed conditional inequalities with cosine floors, k>=b+h, small perturbations, eta and additive errors. A usable full-action doubling statement needs an explicit derivation and error regime; it does not exclude all products.

items.issue: PropositionO1 described as criterion sharpness beyond constants.
items.correction: Its displayed lower bound concerns one specified orbit with explicit j0,Aprime,Delta,kappa. This is not an optimality theorem for every seed criterion or alternative frequency construction. Keep all dependencies when making orbit-lifetime deductions.

items.issue: CorollarySprime numerical shorthand and capped-a case.
items.correction: Roughly L-Lambda>=8 is not a certificate. At the advertised logN=30,gamma=1/2,Lambda=2, left side14 is below the roughly14.1 threshold. Use exact TheoremS inequality. Audit the a=min(1/2,a0) branch before invoking the general corollary; its case-immediate remark is not a supplied derivation.

Floating abs(A)>=1 does not certify a polynomial is nonzero modulo P6 when cancellation is large. Reproducibility is not interval correctness. A proposed seed needs exact reduction and rigorous bounds on all embeddings, cosine floors, infinite tails and strict entropy inequality.
